answers.M6-S1: It's about wanting to grow up tall and worrying about being short. Kids care a lot about how they look compared to their family.
answers.M6-S2: Because it's a magic seed and Billy says the magic won't work if you tell someone. It's like a secret rule for the magic.
answers.M6-S3: The narrator thinks Billy is being nice and generous, but the reader can tell Billy is probably tricking him to get ten cents.
answers.M6-S4: He is really worried about being short like Uncle Alec because Aunt Janet said so, and he wants to be tall really badly.
answers.M6-S5: To make the seed sound more magic and rare and special, so the narrator believes it really works and wants it more.
answers.M6-S6: It shows he is patient and keeps trying the seed. He hasn't grown yet but he still hopes it will work soon.
answers.M6-S7: To show that Billy is tall so the narrator believes the magic seed really works, since Billy says it made him tall.
answers.M6-S8: That people didn't really like Billy that much. He wasn't very popular, maybe because he wasn't always nice or honest.
answers.M6-S9: He likes his uncle a lot, but he doesn't want to be short like him. He wants to grow taller than Uncle Alec.
